issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking possession after alleged dispossession is barred under the applicable possession limitation rule when the plaintiffs fail to establish possession within the relevant preceding period.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sued for a declaration of title and possession, alleging that the defendants had dispossessed them of the land.
The High Court found no evidence that the plaintiffs had been in possession of the land within the twelve years preceding the suit.
The plaintiffs’ counsel could identify no evidence on the record establishing possession within that period.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to hold that the suit was barred under Article 142 of the Limitation Act, 1908.
issues.legal_principle: Article 142 of the Limitation Act, 1908 applied to a suit for possession following alleged dispossession, and the plaintiffs had to establish that they had been in possession within twelve years before instituting the suit.

predicates.possession_suit_after_alleged_dispossess: The plaintiffs brought a suit seeking possession after alleging that they had been dispossessed.
predicates.evidence_of_possession_within_relevant_p: Evidence established that the plaintiffs had possessed the land during the relevant period preceding the suit.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks possession after alleged dispossession and there is no evidence of possession during the relevant preceding period, the suit is barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: Filing a suit within the period associated with a magistrate’s possession order does not prevent the suit from being barred under a separate limitation rule.
material_facts: The plaintiffs contended that their suit was within the three-year period associated with the Magistrate’s order under Section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
The High Court held that Article 47 did not apply because the order was made against individuals, rather than against the plaintiffs in the capacity in which they brought the suit.
The suit sought possession after alleged dispossession, and there was no evidence that the plaintiffs had possessed the land within the twelve years preceding the suit.
issues.conclusion: The suit could be within the limitation period under one article and nevertheless be barred under another; the plaintiffs’ contention based on the Magistrate’s order did not overcome the bar under Article 142.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 47 and 142 of the Limitation Act, 1908 may apply independently, so compliance with the period in one article does not prevent a suit from being barred under another. The Court relied on Jahandad Khan v. Abdul Ghafur Khan and Radhamoni Debi v. The Collector of Khulna (1900) ILR 27 Cal 943 (PC), in which suits brought within three years of orders under Section 145 of the Criminal Procedure Code nevertheless failed under Article 144.

predicates.possession_suit_after_alleged_dispossess: The plaintiffs brought a suit seeking possession after alleging that they had been dispossessed.
predicates.order_based_period_satisfied: The suit was brought within the period associated with a magistrate’s order concerning possession.
predicates.evidence_of_possession_within_relevant_p: Evidence established that the plaintiffs had possessed the land during the relevant period preceding the suit.

issues.definition: Even if a possession suit after alleged dispossession is brought within the period associated with a magistrate’s order, it may remain barred under another limitation rule when there is no evidence of possession during the relevant preceding period.
